answer: A bonded-entry kernel registry resists Sybils by making each voice cost real capital. Every agent locks stake in a shared contract, and the actions it signs are tied to that bond. A Sybil farmer must fund thousands of separate bonds, each fully slashable if the identity is later found colluding, so the price of a fake crowd grows with every clone instead of falling to zero. Lookalike voters can be clustered and their bonds seized together, and reputation stays bound to the stake, so a meadow of fresh agents inherits no trust. A lone raven cannot fake a flock when each wing costs money.
